question: Can visible-history stability predict when selective continuation helps, and does recent refitting remedy old-history oversmoothing?

design.generator: pilot exact family, dominant amplitude8, weak .5 at17.35/128,offset.3,noise.05,decay half-life16,drift+.5 frequency/32 steps
design.refit: last32 only; unthresholded candidate conditional on same full depth1 acceptance; no TEST tuning; residual=x-refitted tone over128

veto.feature: max(norm(latest32-full),norm(latest32-previous32))/norm(full coefficients), fixed full frequency, intercept, absolute phase
veto.fit: Per model minimize mean normalized loss on all FIT seed/cell means; one threshold shared across both periods and all leads/regimes; deterministic ties first grid candidate, native first
veto.test: Freeze selection.json and its hash before opening TEST targets; no TEST feature/outcome tuning

design.loss: MSE / persistent-history variance shared by seed and period across all conditions
primary_hypotheses: H1_Bolt/H1_TimesFM: FIT-only veto improves TEST loss over always native
H2_Bolt/H2_TimesFM: FIT-only veto improves TEST loss over always hybrid
H3_19.2/H3_24: recent-zero improves full-tones-zero on visible changing futures (lead>0,regime!=persistent)
design.primary_scope: Six one-sided sign tests on32 TEST seed-level paired gains; Holm family6; require mean gain>.01 AND adjusted p<=.05. No window/condition pseudoreplication. Native/selector endpoints average all40 balanced cells per seed.
diagnostics: Risk curves per period on lead0 only: no detection claim
Cue gain compares lead0 and cued predictions on the SAME cued future
Recent_hybrid versus hybrid and recent_zero versus tones_zero separates continuation fit from native residual effects
Veto acceptance/benefit per lead/regime/period, reported without TEST threshold selection
Fixed future-mixture probabilities are hypothetical deployment weights, not estimates of pretraining priors
design.uncertainty: 4096 paired source bootstrap percentile95%, seed4953999; intervals descriptive, primary inference via6-test Holm family
design.execution: HOLD until explicit coordinator slot grant; at most1 worker for this track;<=900s/model,CPU1,3GiB,cached/offline,kill on cap; partial artifacts invalid, no subset scoring

exact_findings.status: Completed native replication, FIT-only selector freeze, TEST scoring, and independent audit;4/6 primary screens pass

controls: Every input finite/shape;20 preregistered sentinel histories: exact repeat, capture/plain, three self patches, duplicate singleton calls; both residual repeats. Every abstention exact.
limitations: Prospective synthetic replication; no results yet
Recent refit conditional on full-history acceptance; does not test salvaging abstained cases
Recent32 refit remains a stationary sinusoid; its failure cannot establish that a model ignored a cue.
Exact native replay gates cover20 preregistered sentinel histories rather than every history; all inputs/outputs and abstention identities are still checked.
Runtime estimate comes from pilot geometry; actual replication runtime is unknown. Hard900s/3GiB limits invalidate partial runs.

Hypothetical mixture MSE remains a valid descriptive risk comparison for these point forecasts. It does not identify native training priors or justify treating median outputs as conditional means. Toy MSE-prior training demonstrates a possible mechanism only, not attribution to these TSFMs.

Holm significance is for source-level gain signs, not population-mean improvement. The empirical mean>.01 screen is descriptive; mean bootstrap intervals are uncorrected. Bolt H2 has30/32 wins but two costly observed losses and a mean interval crossing zero.
evidence_class: prospective source-held-out synthetic replication; six corrected primary screens; other slices descriptive

interpretation: FIT-only cutoffs are Bolt0.5 and TimesFM0.1; the actual selection process denied TEST-target reads. No TEST retuning.
Both vetoes pass the preregistered observed mean-gain>.01 plus Holm sign-test screen versus always-hybrid. Neither passes versus native.
Bolt versus native: mean gain0.050279347550187634,19/32 positive sources,Holm p0.37708558747544885; no native-beating primary claim.

TimesFM versus native: mean gain0.035381285186970174,13/32 positive sources,Holm p0.8923364251386374. Its positive mean bootstrap interval does not rescue the failed preregistered sign endpoint; benefits are uneven across sources.

Bolt versus hybrid: mean gain0.024316141847413635,30/32 positives,Holm p3.695022314786911e-07. Its95% mean bootstrap interval[-0.012248115026278854,0.05250180964470645] crosses zero. The sign-based primary passes, but mean gain remains uncertain under source resampling.
TimesFM versus hybrid: mean gain0.11701714686534168,32/32 positives,Holm p1.3969838619232178e-09.

Recent-only tone continuation with zero residual improves visible-changing futures at both periods:19.2 mean gain0.12318180842823585;24 mean gain0.11615768959478193;32/32 positives each;Holm p1.3969838619232178e-09 each. This is controlled evidence that the fitting window contributes to continuation error in this generator.

Recent refitting is not a general native hybrid remedy: TEST all-cell recent_hybrid losses0.6020191756973894 Bolt and0.6046294010530298 TimesFM; corresponding native losses0.7975724959262678 and0.5677474183322653. These are secondary descriptive comparisons, not additional corrected primary claims.

Native and native-residual outputs are medians, not means. Hypothetical MSE risk remains valid for these forecasts but cannot identify their training priors. Toy squared-loss prior results are possible mechanisms, not attribution to these TSFMs.
statistical_interpretation: Inference scope: the one-sided sign test concerns P(source-level gain > 0 | nonzero gain) > 0.5. It does not test whether the population mean gain is positive.

The preregistered pass flag combines an OBSERVED sample mean gain > 0.01 with a Holm-corrected sign test. The empirical mean threshold is not a significance test of the population mean. A pass must not be described as statistically significant population-mean improvement.
Source-bootstrap intervals describe uncertainty in the mean separately; they are descriptive and uncorrected, and do not replace the preregistered sign endpoint.

Observed Bolt H2 downside risk: 30/32 positive sources, but two observed losses [-0.3868321842787914, -0.17470621984158152]; mean bootstrap95% interval [-0.012248115026278854, 0.05250180964470645] crosses zero. Frequent wins coexist with costly losses; the sign-based screen passes while population-mean improvement is not established.
TimesFM H1: observed mean gain 0.035381285186970174, but only 13/32 positive sources; H1 fails. A positive descriptive mean interval does not rescue its failed sign endpoint.

H3 passes at both periods with32/32 positive TEST sources each. Its sign-test significance concerns source-level win probability, not population-mean improvement; sample means and descriptive intervals remain separate evidence.
